result:
Fixed. The 400s came from the client building query strings without percent-encoding, and the fix is in place with regression tests.

**Root cause.** `_build_url` in `src/api_client.py` joined query parameters with raw string formatting. Any account name containing a space or `&` produced a request target that is invalid under RFC 3986, and the origin rejected it with 400. That is why only "some users" were affected: those whose account names contain such characters, for example "Acme Holdings" or "Smith & Co".

**Why reports looked healthy.** The reports endpoint is on the retry list, so its 400 was retried and landed on the legacy-proxy edge node, which re-quotes the target before forwarding. The retry masked the bug rather than the endpoint being correct. It also hid a data bug: an `&` in the account name split the query, so reports for "Smith & Co" silently returned an empty list instead of the account's data.

**Changes made.**
- `src/api_client.py`: the query string is now built with `urlencode` using percent-encoding, so reserved characters in values can no longer corrupt the target. The export id in `get_export` is also percent-encoded as a path segment, since it had the same class of defect.
- `tests/test_api_client.py`: added six regression tests covering exports, reports, and account search with spaces and ampersands, plus path-segment encoding for single-export lookups.

**Verification.** All 19 tests pass with the fix. I also ran the new tests against the original code with the fix stashed, and all six fail there with the same 400 seen in the bug report, which confirms they catch the regression.

**One thing to consider.** The retry-on-400 behaviour for reports is what hid this defect. A 400 is normally a permanent client error, so retrying it is unusual. I left it unchanged because existing tests specify it, but it may be worth reviewing separately.

The changes are uncommitted in the working tree.
